tested_scope: Current Chat GitHub connector schema discovery for issue-comment reaction create/list/remove plus official GitHub REST Reactions, GitHub Actions workflow-event, and REST rate-limit documentation retrieved 2026-09-12 JST. No issue/comment/reaction mutation was performed.

public_evidence.source: GitHub Docs - REST API endpoints for reactions
public_evidence.claim: For create reaction on an issue comment, HTTP 200 means the same authenticated actor already added that reaction type; 201 means created. Reaction content is restricted to eight values. List reactions exposes reaction IDs; delete removes by reaction_id.

public_evidence.source: GitHub Docs - Events that trigger workflows
public_evidence.claim: The documented issue_comment workflow event covers comment created, edited, and deleted activity. No reaction event is documented on that workflow-trigger page; therefore the reaction mutation itself has no documented Actions trigger in this tested scope. Creating or deleting the target comment, however, can trigger issue_comment workflows.

public_evidence.source: GitHub Docs - Rate limits for the REST API
public_evidence.claim: GitHub REST uses hourly primary limits and secondary per-minute/content-generation limits; rate-limit failure is recoverable across invocations and is not a monthly/trial/paid-credit dependency.

findings.same_actor_same_target_same_content_dupl: pass_exact_scope: repeat create is explicitly distinguished as existing (200) versus created (201)
findings.ambiguous_write_reconciliation: pass_exact_scope: retrying the same tuple cannot create a second same-actor/same-content reaction; list returns reaction records including id for exact cleanup
findings.cleanup: pass_exact_scope: current Chat connector exposes remove by reaction_id and official REST supports delete
findings.workflow_trigger_risk_for_required_targe: unresolved_or_nonzero_if_a_new_issue_comment_must_be_created; issue_comment create/delete can trigger workflows and therefore hosted-runner/quota usage
findings.caller_controlled_unique_identity: fail_generic: identity is effectively repository + existing comment_id + authenticated actor + one of only eight reaction contents; the caller cannot encode an arbitrary unbounded operation key on one stable target
findings.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: 0_under_tested_scope; only ordinary GitHub REST rate limits/secondary limits observed
findings.residual_bootstrap_dependency: requires a pre-existing stable issue comment target; manufacturing fresh targets would broaden into comment-creation semantics with workflow-trigger risk

counterexample: Although reaction creation has unusually strong idempotent duplicate semantics and Chat-exposed exact list/delete, a fixed target offers only eight caller-selectable reaction values per authenticated actor. Arbitrary operation-key uniqueness therefore requires additional target comments or other namespace expansion; provisioning those targets can trigger issue_comment workflows and reintroduce hosted-runner/quota risk. The primitive is useful as a tiny bounded semaphore/token on an already-existing stable comment, not as the generic server-side durable operation-key record required here.
